description: Seven-category QA checklist for qwen2.5vl:7b vision model semantic validation of rendered 3D world scenes.

categories.name: Geometry Accuracy
categories.prompt: Are the 3D object shapes geometrically correct and proportionate? Check for distorted meshes, missing faces, or obviously wrong proportions.

categories.name: Object Count
categories.prompt: Does the scene contain the expected number of distinct objects as described in the conversation? Are there missing objects or unexpected duplicates?

categories.name: Camera Placement
categories.prompt: Is the camera positioned at a natural eye-level first-person view? Is the scene composed from a reasonable vantage point with appropriate framing?

categories.name: Openings & Portals
categories.prompt: Are doors, windows, archways, and other openings correctly placed and proportioned? Do openings connect spaces logically and appear traversable?

categories.name: Surface Finish
categories.prompt: Do surfaces have appropriate materials and textures? Check for missing textures (solid pink/magenta), obvious tiling artifacts, or incorrect material assignments.

categories.name: Mood & Lighting
categories.prompt: Does the lighting convey the intended mood from the conversation? Is the scene appropriately lit without extreme overexposure or pitch-black areas?

categories.name: Scale Consistency
categories.prompt: Are objects scaled consistently relative to each other and to human proportions? Check for furniture that is too large/small, doors that are unrealistic heights, etc.

system_prompt: You are a 3D scene quality assurance inspector. You evaluate rendered 3D world screenshots against a structured checklist. For each category, determine if the rendered scene passes or fails. Be strict but fair — minor imperfections are acceptable, but structural issues should fail. Respond ONLY with valid JSON.

verdict_schema.pass: boolean — true if all categories pass, false if any category fails
verdict_schema.failed_checks: array of category IDs that failed (empty array if pass is true)
verdict_schema.confidence: float 0.0-1.0 — your confidence in the overall verdict
